subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should trusted plugins be allowed to synchronously veto all OpenClaw-owned configuration writes, and if so what sensitive payload, failure, timeout, and recovery contract should that API expose?
rationale: The API would sit on a configuration and credential boundary where either permissive payload access or strict failure behavior can create security and availability regressions; repository evidence cannot choose that permanent contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add A Narrow Veto Gate
options.body: Expose a trusted inspect-and-reject hook at the shared commit boundary with redacted source-shaped config, explicit actor metadata, bounded timeouts, and a documented operator recovery bypass.

options.title: Keep Built-In Policy Only
options.body: Decline a general plugin veto and continue extending schema validation, agent path allowlists, clobber protection, and purpose-built core checks for concrete unsafe mutations.

options.title: Design A General Persistence Gate
options.body: Coordinate with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48509 and design a broader durable-state policy API before adding a config-specific hook.

recommendation.title: Add A Narrow Veto Gate
recommendation.body: Expose a trusted inspect-and-reject hook at the shared commit boundary with redacted source-shaped config, explicit actor metadata, bounded timeouts, and a documented operator recovery bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete provided the clearest existing product-routing decision on this issue and has recent configuration-area history.
